title: 2d — Building a Tiny Game

content.title: You Have Everything You Need
content.summary: input, variables, print, if, and else — that's enough to build a real game.
content.body:
Look at what you can do now:

• input() — ask the player a question
• variables — remember their answers
• print() — show messages and story
• if / else — make choices and branch the story

That's not just code. That's a game engine. Let's build something with it.

content.title: A Complete Tiny Game
content.summary: All the pieces together: ask → store → decide → react.
content.body:
door = input("Choose a door: red or blue? ")

if door == "red":
    print("You open the red door...")
    print("A dragon is napping inside. It opens one eye.")
    print("The dragon goes back to sleep. You tiptoe past.")
else:
    print("You open the blue door...")
    print("Treasure! Mountains of gold coins!")
    print("You fill your pockets and sneak out.")

The whole thing is only 8 lines — but it's a real game with two completely different stories.

content.title: Multiple print() Lines Inside if/else
content.summary: You can have as many lines as you want inside if or else — just keep them all indented.
content.body: You can put as many print() lines as you like inside an if or else — as long as they're all indented. Each indented line runs only for that branch. The moment a line goes back to the edge, it's outside the if/else and runs always.

content.title: Make It Yours
content.summary: The best games have personality. Give yours a setting, some humour, and a twist.
content.body:
The starter code is just a starting point. Swap out the story, change the choices, add a character name. The best games have personality — weird twists, funny moments, unexpected outcomes.

Ideas:
• Cave adventure with a sleeping troll
• Wizard duel where both spells go wrong
• Spaceship with a broken teleporter
• A guessing game with a sassy robot

You're the author. Make it fun.

editorPrompt: Build a tiny game using input, variables, if, else, and print.
progressiveHints:
# Hint: ask the player's name first so you can use it in the story!
# name = input("What is your name, adventurer? ")
# print("Welcome, " + name + "!")

name = input("What is your name? ")
door = input("Choose a door: red or blue? ")

if door == "red":
    print(name + " opens the red door...")
    print("A friendly dragon waves hello!")
else:
    print(name + " opens the blue door...")
    print("A treasure chest gleams in the dark!")

name = input("What is your name? ")
print("Welcome, " + name + "! Your adventure begins now.")

path = input("Do you enter the forest or the castle? ")

if path == "forest":
    print("The trees whisper your name...")
    print("A tiny fox hands you a magic acorn.")
else:
    print("The castle gates creak open.")
    print("A ghost butler offers you a snack.")
challenge: 🚀 Dive Deeper: Ask the player their name AND a choice. Use the name in your story text so it feels personal. Add at least 3 print() lines to each branch to make the story really come alive!
